player_0.content: New plan: I failed to achieve the target state because I selected option (C) "Ambiguous" for the final sentence, which was incorrect. The pronoun "his" in the sentence "Bailey planned to meet the director at his office" refers to **Bailey**, as it is standard English convention for a person to meet someone at their own office unless specified otherwise. My strategy incorrectly assumed ambiguity where there was a clear pragmatic antecedent. Next time, I will analyze the semantic context of the sentence to determine if the pronoun naturally refers to the subject (Bailey) or the object (the director) based on common usage, rather than defaulting to ambiguity. Specifically, I should recognize that "meet the director at his office" implies the director's office only if the director is the one hosting, but the sentence structure "Bailey planned to meet..." strongly suggests Bailey is the one going to the director's location, making "his" refer to Bailey. I will select option (B) for this type of sentence.
